statement_tested: VF-25 (reworded). Loading the system reveals MCI where the unloaded or static counterpart does not. Within the same study, a measure taken under a more demanding condition (for example dual-task or curved-path walking, peripheral-attention reaction time, or task-evoked responses), or a microstructural index of a structure (for example diffusion measures), separates MCI from a non-impaired comparator. The same measure under the simpler condition, or the corresponding volume, does not.
encoding_note: File kept ASCII. In quotations the source's minus sign is written '-', plus-minus '+/-', the Greek beta in 'A-beta-neg/pos' as 'Abeta', and the en dash as '-'. Nothing else in the quotations is altered.

results.loaded_measure: Whole-white-matter free-water fraction (f-index) from single-shell free-water DTI (ROI over the entire white matter, ComBat-harmonised, ANCOVA with Tukey post hoc)
results.simpler_or_static_measure: Whole-brain white-matter volume (% of brain, ANTs Atropos segmentation of T1), the corresponding volume of the same structure; Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn-Bonferroni
results.comparator: Cognitively normal (CN) adults: 472 in the diffusion analysis, 469 in volumetry. MCI groups: ADNI early MCI (136 diffusion / 135 volumetry) and late MCI (60 / 60)
results.dataset_family: ADNI (single-shell 3T diffusion subset, multi-scanner Siemens/GE, ComBat-harmonised); 472 CN, 136 EMCI, 60 LMCI after motion exclusion
results.method_family: Single-shell two-compartment free-water DTI (f-index, fw-FA, fw-AX, fw-RD; voxelwise TFCE plus whole-WM ROI) set against ANTs Atropos tissue-fraction volumetry (WM, GM, CSF)
results.why: Identity: the PDF (Bergamino, McElvogue, Stokes and ADNI, NeuroSci 2025, 6, 8) matches the summaries.md header of Paper 566; the text was read in full to the end of the references. PART SHOWN: for CN versus early MCI, in essentially the same participants (volumetry lost 3 CN and 1 EMCI for lack of T1), the whole-white-matter free-water fraction separates the groups (CN 0.294 +/- 0.041 vs EMCI 0.321 +/- 0.042; t = -6.822, p < 0.001) while the corresponding volume, whole-brain WM volume, does not (33.4 (2.7) vs 33.3 (2.7) %; Dunn Z = 0.54, p = 1.00). That is a diffusion index of a structure against the corresponding volume of the same structure, against a non-impaired comparator, with the static null coming from a large sample (469 vs 135), so it is not a small-sample null. WHY PARTLY AND NOT YES: the dissociation holds only for one of the study's two MCI groups. For CN versus late MCI the f-index separates (t = -4.128, p < 0.001) but WM volume also separates (Z = 5.12, p < 0.001), so for LMCI there is no dissociation. By the brief's subgroup rule the answer is partly. The study never pools MCI against CN, so MCI as a whole is not shown. CAVEATS (not disqualifiers under the reworded rules): (1) The authors never contrast the two measure types; the dissociation is assembled from Tables 7 and 8, and their own summary reads the volumes as separating ('Volumetric analyses revealed reduced white and gray matter volumes ... in the MCI groups'), although Section 3.6 correctly confines WM reduction to LMCI. (2) Other static measures separate the same CN-EMCI contrast: GM volume (Z = 4.35, p < 0.001) and CSF volume (Z = -3.92, p < 0.001). Neither is the corresponding volume of white matter, so under the reworded statement this is a caveat, not a 'no'. (3) The index that succeeds is the extracellular free-water fraction, which the authors tie to CSF increase from neuronal loss (p.2); CSF volume separated the same groups, and the whole-WM mask derivation is not described, so CSF partial-volume at WM borders cannot be excluded. The tissue-microstructure indices at the same whole-WM scale (fw-FA F = 0.101, p = 0.904; fw-AX p = 0.543; fw-RD p = 0.676) separate no pair; fw-FA separates only in voxelwise TFCE clusters, which are not spatially matched to whole-WM volume. (4) The two arms were analysed differently: diffusion metrics ComBat-harmonised with age, sex and motion then ANCOVA/Tukey; volumes by unadjusted Kruskal-Wallis/Dunn on percentage volumes with no stated scanner harmonisation, while sex differs (CN 282/472 female, EMCI 54/136). (5) No measure-by-group interaction test. (6) Single-shell fw-DTI, which the authors name as the main limitation; multi-scanner data; ADNI EMCI/LMCI split rests on one Logical Memory II story (authors' limitation). (7) The authors' emphasised contrast, EMCI versus LMCI, has no non-impaired comparator and is not used here. INDEPENDENCE: ADNI. No overlap with the current supporters (P-651 Chongqing, P-661 UT Dallas/UTSW, P-662 Shanghai Tongji, P-665/P-687 one Guangzhou sample, P-666 Wuhan Tongji) or with P-1425 (BABRI). If any other ADNI paper were admitted, ADNI would count once and an all-ADNI exception would need declaring. Method note: the discriminating index is a free-water fraction, conceptually close to P-651's NODDI FISO (both isotropic-fluid fractions), though the acquisition and model differ (single-shell fw-DTI vs multi-shell NODDI). Not a registry duplicate stub; peer-reviewed, not a preprint.
results.caveats: Holds for CN vs EMCI only; in CN vs LMCI WM volume also separates. GM and CSF volumes separate CN vs EMCI. Succeeding index is the free-water fraction (fluid), not tissue anisotropy; whole-WM fw-FA/AX/RD fail. The dissociation is assembled from Tables 7-8, not stated by the authors. The arms were analysed with different pipelines (harmonised and covariate-adjusted vs unadjusted nonparametric). No interaction test. Single-shell, multi-scanner ADNI.

quotes.quote: Significant group differences were identified in the f-index metric (CN vs. EMCI: t = -6.822, p < 0.001; CN vs. LMCI: t = -4.128, p < 0.001).
For white matter, volume reductions were identified in the LMCI group, with significant differences between the CN and LMCI groups and between EMCI and LMCI.
Three CN individuals and one EMCI individual were excluded from this analysis due to the unavailability of structural images.
Volumetric analyses revealed reduced white and gray matter volumes and increased CSF volumes in the MCI groups.

Group differences for age, for all cognitive tests (MMSE, GDS, CDR, and FAQ), and for regional brain volumes were evaluated using the Kruskal-Wallis test followed by the Dunn test corrected by the Bonferroni procedure due to non-normality
This process incorporated biological variables such as sex, age, and subject motion.
AD is characterized by neuronal loss, which leads to increased cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and fw across the brain.
The main limitation of the study is related to the single-shell dMRI acquisition.

results.loaded_measure: Atlas-based DTI fractional anisotropy and mean diffusivity in 20 JHU white-matter tract ROIs (30-direction single-shell DTI, PANDA; ANCOVA with age, sex, education)
results.simpler_or_static_measure: Whole-brain voxel-based morphometry of grey-matter volume (SPM12, voxelwise p < 0.001 uncorrected then FWE p < 0.05). No white-matter or tract volume is analysed, so the corresponding volume of the tracts is not tested
results.comparator: 32 normal controls (age, sex and education matched to both MCI groups) vs 19 amyloid-negative MCI and 18 amyloid-positive MCI (florbetapir visual read)
results.dataset_family: BABRI (Beijing Aging Brain Rejuvenation Initiative) community cohort, Beijing Normal University; 3T Prisma MRI at the BNU Imaging Center for Brain Research; not public
results.method_family: Atlas-based single-shell tensor DTI (FA/MD, JHU atlas ROIs, ROI ANCOVA) set against whole-brain SPM12 VBM of grey-matter volume; florbetapir PET for amyloid grouping
results.why: Identity: the PDF (Dai, Zhang, ... Peng, Zhang, Front Neurol 2026, 16:1658712) matches the summaries.md header of Paper 1425; the text was read in full to the end of the references. PART SHOWN: in amyloid-negative MCI versus matched normal controls, diffusion measures of white-matter tracts separate the groups (lower FA in bilateral cingulum cingulate and hippocampal parts, ILF, right ATR, IFOF, left UF, forceps minor, plus left CT and right UF; higher MD in most of 16 tracts; marked as NC vs Abeta-neg differences after correction in Figure 2), while whole-brain VBM finds no grey-matter atrophy that survives FWE ('an atrophy trend ... did not reach statistical significance'). The authors state the split themselves ('both MCI subgroups showed widespread WM tract disruptions, whereas significant GM atrophy was observed only in the Abeta-pos MCI group'). Same participants, non-impaired comparator, groups matched on age (p = 0.459), sex (p = 0.802) and education (p = 0.064). WHY PARTLY AND NOT YES: (1) Subgroup only. In amyloid-positive MCI the static measure also separates (bilateral hippocampal and left parahippocampal atrophy), and MCI as a whole is never compared with NC, so the dissociation holds only in the 19-patient amyloid-negative subgroup, which the authors describe as heterogeneous with possible non-AD pathology. By the brief's subgroup rule the answer is partly. (2) The static measure is not the corresponding volume. White-matter tract diffusion is set against grey-matter volume; no WM or tract volume is analysed, and no hippocampal-volume ROI test for Abeta-neg MCI vs NC is reported (left-HIP GMV appears only in correlations and the all-participant mediation model). The study therefore shows a diffusion-versus-GM-volume dissociation, which is part of, not the whole of, 'the corresponding volume does not'. If the operator reads 'corresponding volume' strictly, this ground alone would leave the corresponding-structure half undemonstrated. CAVEATS: (3) The two arms were tested at different stringency: whole-brain voxelwise VBM with FWE correction versus ANCOVA on 20 atlas ROIs with post hoc tests described as FDR-corrected in Methods (p.3) and Bonferroni-corrected in the Figure 2 caption (p.5), an internal inconsistency; the less stringent ROI test favours the diffusion arm. (4) The VBM null is a threshold null reported in words only, with no statistic; covariates and TIV are not stated for the VBM. (5) The pairwise DTI results are given only as figure superscripts and in Supplementary Table S2 (not in the extract), with no t, p or effect size in the text. (6) No measure-by-group interaction test. (7) Small groups (19 vs 32); cross-sectional; not every NC had PET (authors' limitation). INDEPENDENCE: BABRI, Beijing. No cohort, site or author overlap with the current supporters (P-651 Chongqing, P-661 UT Dallas/UTSW, P-662 Shanghai Tongji, P-665/P-687 one Guangzhou sample, P-666 Wuhan Tongji) or with P-566 (ADNI). BABRI is also the cohort of P-981, a previously rejected VF-25 supporter (a different, longitudinal study of the same community cohort); that paper is not a supporter, so no double count arises, but the two would be one dataset family if P-981 were ever admitted. METHOD FAMILY: tensor FA/MD with JHU atlas ROIs is the same method family as current supporter P-666 (DTI, TBSS plus ICBM atlas ROI; round 20: no), distinct from P-651's multi-shell NODDI. Not a registry duplicate stub; peer-reviewed, not a preprint.
results.caveats: Holds only in amyloid-negative MCI (n = 19); in amyloid-positive MCI GM volume also separates. The static measure is GM volume, not the corresponding WM volume. Unequal stringency (whole-brain FWE VBM vs 20-ROI ANCOVA; FDR vs Bonferroni stated inconsistently). VBM null reported without statistics. Pairwise DTI statistics only as figure superscripts/supplement. No interaction test. Small, cross-sectional; not all NC had PET.

quotes.quote: Specifically, post-hoc analyses found that both Abetaneg MCI and Abetapos MCI patients showed decreased FA in the bilateral cingulum cingulate gyrus part (CCG), cingulum hippocampus part (CH), inferior longitudinal fasciculus (ILF), right anterior thalamic radiation (ATR), inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus (IFOF), left uncinate fasciculus (UF), and forceps minor (FMIN).
In addition, Abetaneg MCI showed lower FA in the left corticospinal tract (CT) and right UF
Similarly, the two MCI subgroups showed extensive increased MD in 16 of the 20 WM tract ROIs.
Statistically significant differences after Bonferroni correction are marked with superscripts. aPost-hoc paired comparisons showed significant group differences between NC and Abetaneg MCI.
Relative to NC, Abetapos MCI showed significant atrophy in the bilateral hippocampus (HIP) and left parahippocampus. (sentence begins on page 4)

In the Abetaneg MCI group, an atrophy trend was observed in the right supramarginal gyrus, inferior temporal gyri, left temporal pole, and fusiform gyrus; however, these changes did not reach statistical significance.
In summary, both MCI subgroups showed widespread WM tract disruptions, whereas significant GM atrophy was observed only in the Abetapos MCI group.
The threshold for the resulting statistical parametric maps was established at p < 0.001 (uncorrected) and then family-wise error (FWE) corrected for multiple comparisons at p < 0.05.
Moreover, the Post-hoc pairwise t-tests were conducted for those significant ANCOVA results after FDR correction.
an atlas-based approach was applied to extract regional diffusion metrics, including fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD), across 20 WM tracts.
There were no statistically significant differences in age, sex, or education among the three groups.
This study found significant WM damage in both Abetapos and Abetaneg MCI groups, while notable GM atrophy was only observed in the Abetapos MCI group.

Although Abetaneg MCI usually represents a heterogeneous population characterized by various non-AD pathophysiological processes, such as cerebrovascular injury, TDP-43 pathology, or age-related neurodegeneration
Lastly, not all NC participants underwent PET scan, which may have partially influenced the characterization of Abetapos and Abetaneg MCI subgroups.

summary: Both papers stay partly under the reworded statement. P-566 (ADNI): whole-WM free-water fraction separates CN from early MCI where whole-WM volume does not (t = -6.822 vs Dunn Z = 0.54, p = 1.00), but for late MCI WM volume also separates (Z = 5.12), so the dissociation holds in one MCI subgroup only. P-1425 (BABRI): tract DTI separates amyloid-negative MCI from NC where whole-brain GM VBM does not, but in amyloid-positive MCI GM volume also separates, and the static measure is GM rather than the corresponding WM volume. Neither shares a sample with a current supporter or with each other.
